source: SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 generic DTC definitions (built-in reference)

symptoms: Driver frontal airbag may not deploy
Horn or wheel controls may fail too
codes.notes: SRS work requires following OEM disable/enable procedures: disconnect the battery and wait the OEM-specified time before disconnecting any SRS component, use the OEM-specified load tool or simulator, and never probe or measure resistance directly across an inflator or pretensioner with a meter or test light. After repair, enable the system per OEM procedure and confirm the SRS lamp completes its bulb check and goes out. Clockspring (spiral cable) faults are common, especially when steering wheel controls or the horn fail at the same time. Use the OEM load tool at each connector to isolate the faulty section. Generic SAE J2012 base DTC, normally reported with a failure-type byte (for example -11 short to ground, -12 short to battery, -13 circuit open). Some older vehicles, notably older GM models, assign manufacturer-specific meanings to B0 codes; confirm with OEM service information.

causes: Sensor left unplugged after front-end repair
Sensor or mount damaged in collision
Harness or connector damage or corrosion
codes.notes: SRS work requires following OEM disable/enable procedures: disconnect the battery and wait the OEM-specified time before disconnecting any SRS component, use the OEM-specified load tool or simulator, and never probe or measure resistance directly across an inflator or pretensioner with a meter or test light. After repair, enable the system per OEM procedure and confirm the SRS lamp completes its bulb check and goes out. Mount sensors exactly as specified by the OEM. Generic SAE J2012 base DTC, normally reported with a failure-type byte (for example -11 short to ground, -12 short to battery, -13 circuit open). causes: Occupant classification sensor or mat fault
Objects under or on the passenger seat
Seat damage or aftermarket seat cover
codes.notes: SRS work requires following OEM disable/enable procedures: disconnect the battery and wait the OEM-specified time before disconnecting any SRS component, use the OEM-specified load tool or simulator, and never probe or measure resistance directly across an inflator or pretensioner with a meter or test light. Many occupant classification systems require a rezero or calibration with a scan tool after seat or sensor service, performed with the seat empty per OEM procedure. Never modify or bypass occupant classification components. symptoms: ABS pump does not run on self-test
causes: Pump motor fuse or power feed fault
codes.notes: Voltage-drop test the high-current fuse, main power feed, and ground while the pump is commanded on, if the scan tool supports a pump test. On many units the pump motor and module are serviced as an assembly, and hydraulic unit replacement usually requires an OEM scan-tool bleed procedure. Generic SAE J2012 base DTC, normally reported with a failure-type byte that narrows the fault. Many older vehicles (for example older GM and Toyota models) use C0 codes with manufacturer-specific meanings; confirm the definition in OEM service information for the vehicle.

symptoms: Possible false ABS activation at low speed
codes.notes: Compare all four wheel speeds on a scan tool during a road test to find signal dropouts. Inspect the harness where it flexes with suspension travel, check the tone ring and wheel bearing, and verify sensor output (AC voltage for passive sensors or a square-wave or current signal for active sensors) per OEM procedure. Generic SAE J2012 base DTC, normally reported with a failure-type byte that narrows the fault. Many older vehicles (for example older GM and Toyota models) use C0 codes with manufacturer-specific meanings; confirm the definition in OEM service information for the vehicle.

causes: Wiring or connector fault at column
codes.notes: After a wheel alignment, steering component replacement, or battery disconnect, many systems require a steering angle sensor calibration with a scan tool. Where the sensor is part of the clockspring, SRS work requires following OEM disable/enable procedures before the driver airbag or clockspring is disturbed. Generic SAE J2012 base DTC, normally reported with a failure-type byte that narrows the fault. Many older vehicles (for example older GM and Toyota models) use C0 codes with manufacturer-specific meanings; confirm the definition in OEM service information for the vehicle.
